messages:
alice: Heads-up: kicking off migration add_customer_flags to prod canary at 1% now. pinning service to a known-good build.
deploybot: Deploy started: migration=add_customer_flags canary=1% deploy_id=deploy-2024-11-01-phi
ben: Quick Q — does this create a concurrent index that can take locks? any FK validations?
dba_mike: No FK changes. Index is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on customers(flags_idx). should avoid table locks but backfill writes may cause bloat. expected IO spike ~2-4%.
carol: Also, which service SHA is being pinned? need to coordinate the feature flag rollout with traffic split.
alice: Pinning service to service@f9c3e2 (rollout build). feature flag will be rolled from 0->10% after canary passes.
rachel_oncall: Change window: 23:00-02:00 UTC. If any long-lived locks > 2m, abort and hold. Oncall will escalate to DBA.
sara_prod: Added release notes link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RD-5324 — includes migration steps and rollback scripts.
ben: Rollback plan captured here. if we abort:
```
# stop the migration deploy
deploybot cancel deploy-2024-11-01-phi
# run the rollback script on primary within maintenance window
scripts/migrations/rollback_add_customer_flags.sh --target=primary
```
carol: Suggest adding a guarded quiesce: if table_lock_waits > 5s for > 3 hosts, fail canary.
dba_mike: Agree. I'll add a DB metric alert: metric=db.lock_wait_seconds[customers] threshold=5s duration=3m -> action=abort-deploy.
alice: Can we run the backfill on replica and stream changes? avoids primaries being noisy.
dba_mike: We'll backfill on read-replicas then sync with logical replication. latency estimate ~8-10m for 1% subset.
ben: Reaction :thumbsup:
sara_prod: Noted to mention cost spike in release notes.
deploybot: Canary update: 1% completed, no lock-time alerts. monitoring window=15m. next check at +10m.
